title: A punctured root chart commutes with one ring base change
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, b:R → S a ring homomorphism, f an element of R, and n a natural number. Write A_R=R[T]/(T^n-f), A_S=S[T]/(T^n-b(f)), q_R:Spec A_R → Spec R and q_S:Spec A_S → Spec S for the structural maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put V_R=D(f) inside Spec A_R and V_S=D(b(f)) inside Spec A_S, with their open inclusions i_R and i_S. There is an isomorphism e:V_S ≅ Spec S ×_{Spec R} V_R, where the pullback uses Spec b and i_R;q_R, such that e followed by the first projection equals i_S;q_S. There are no regularity, positivity, nonzero-ring or nonzero-coefficient assumptions.

source.place: Polynomial quotient base change implicit in Tag 05N9; lem-sbc-punctured-root-colimit-continuity step 1; Mathlib AdjoinRoot.lift, AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root, isPullback_SpecMap_of_isPushout, isPullback_morphismRestrict. The explicit universal-property argument is written and fully proved by J1.

proof.text: For arbitrary p in R[T] and q=p.map(b), prove the canonical square R → S, AdjoinRoot p → AdjoinRoot q is a pushout. For a cocone to C, lift the S-map using the image of root(p) under the other cocone leg. The cocone equation and eval₂_root show q vanishes there. The lift has the required coefficient and root formulas; these formulas also prove uniqueness. This is the private Lean theorem root_pushout, proved without dependencies beyond Mathlib.

Specialize p to T^n-f, take Spec of the pushout and identify the inverse image of D(f) with D(b(f)) by AdjoinRoot.map_of. Paste the basic-open restriction pullback square with the root-chart pullback square. Its isoPullback comparison and first-projection identity give the required isomorphism and equality.
